content.user_title: Map Complex Work Across Issue Tickets
content.value_statement: Large ambiguous projects can exceed one AI session and lose decisions across conversations. Wayfinder turns the work into an issue-tracker map with focused tickets.
actual_capabilities: Creates a map issue labeled wayfinder:map for a large effort.
Defines child tickets for research, prototype, grilling, and task work.
Uses blocking relationships to identify the open frontier of work.
Records unresolved uncertainty in a Fog section until it becomes actionable.
Guides agents to claim and resolve one ticket per session.
Adds resolved decisions back to the map as short linked pointers.
limitations: Requires an issue tracker or a local Markdown tracker convention.
Depends on repository-specific tracker instructions when they exist.
Does not complete multiple tickets in a single agent session.
Does not replace human review of project priorities or final decisions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Large Engineering Initiative
use_cases.description: Break a broad technical goal into research, prototype, and implementation tickets that can be handled across sessions.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Parallel Investigation
use_cases.description: Use issue assignments and blocking relationships so several agents or people can work without duplicating effort.

use_cases.title: Preserve Decisions Over Time
use_cases.description: Keep a durable map of resolved decisions and remaining uncertainty while a project moves through changing context.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a broad idea that needs structure.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wayfinder to chart this project as an issue-tracker map: [describe the goal]. Identify the first tickets and the fog.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve the Next Ticket
prompt_templates.scenario: Continue an existing map without choosing a ticket manually.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wayfinder with this map: [map link]. Pick the first unblocked and unclaimed ticket, claim it, and resolve only that ticket.

prompt_templates.title: Add Tracker-Specific Structure
prompt_templates.scenario: Adapt the map to the repository issue tracker.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wayfinder for [project]. Follow this repository's issue tracker rules, create typed child tickets, and wire blocking relationships.

prompt_templates.title: Advance a Complex Program
prompt_templates.scenario: Maintain a long-running map after a decision changes future work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use wayfinder on [map link]. Resolve [ticket name], update Decisions so far, graduate new fog into tickets, and revise invalidated tickets.

output_examples.input: Plan a migration from a legacy billing flow to a new payment provider.
output: A map issue for the migration effort.
Research tickets for provider APIs and compliance questions.
Prototype tickets for checkout behavior and failure states.
Fog notes for pricing, rollout, and support decisions.

output_examples.input: Continue this map and take the next available work item.
output: The next unblocked ticket is claimed.
The ticket is resolved with a linked answer or asset.
The map gains a short decision pointer.
Newly visible follow-up tickets are added.

best_practices: Keep each ticket small enough for one focused agent session.
Use clear ticket names so links remain readable in map summaries.
Record only short decision pointers on the map and keep details in tickets.
anti_patterns: Do not resolve tickets during the same session that creates the map.
Do not paste full ticket answers into the map body.
Do not create precise tickets for uncertainty that still belongs in Fog.

faq.question: What does Wayfinder create?
faq.answer: It creates an issue-based map with child tickets, decision pointers, and fog for unresolved uncertainty.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub Issues?
faq.answer: No. It expects an issue tracker pattern and can fall back to local Markdown when tracker guidance is absent.

faq.question: Can several agents use the same map?
faq.answer: Yes. Tickets are claimed by assignment so parallel sessions can avoid taking the same work.

faq.question: Why does it limit work to one ticket per session?
faq.answer: The limit keeps context focused and makes each resolution easy to audit, link, and continue.

faq.question: What is Fog?
faq.answer: Fog is the map section for likely future questions that cannot yet be written as precise tickets.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
